evidence_rule: Every gate cites segment IDs of the hash-checked retained article text in the screen directory; quotes must occur verbatim inside the cited segment. Original code, repositories and author implementations were not consulted.
pilot_eligibility_rule: A candidate is a provisional pilot case only if article text is lawfully retained, primary G1 = yes and primary G2 != no. Candidates failing this rule are replaced by the next candidate in deterministic order within the same stratum; every skipped candidate and reason is retained here. G3/G4/G5 never cause replacement (access and specification failures are study outcomes).

deviation.protocol_clause: protocols/PROTOCOL.md: 'human adjudication against the retained bytes is required before any gate is recorded'
deviation.description: Initial G1-G5 adjudication of pilot candidates was performed by Devin from the retained bytes instead of the author. The author will verify or overturn each gate afterwards. Records below are therefore provisional; the formal funnel file remains NOT_STARTED until author verification is recorded.
deviation.consequence: Pilot selection derived from these gates is provisional. If author verification changes a gate that affects eligibility, the affected stratum must be re-selected before any blind run using that stratum is counted.

assessments.G1_reason: Central claims are wet-lab outcomes: colony pigmentation of 42 strains on a new differential medium. The ML phylogeny (ClustalW/MEGA X) only supports strain identification and is not a central claim.
assessments.alternatives_considered: cpn60/16S maximum-likelihood phylogeny (MEGA X 10.2.4, GTR+G+I) considered and rejected as ancillary identification, not a central claim.

evidence.quote: formed yellow or orange colonies on the differential medium
by MEGAX (10.2.4) was then used to generate a Maximum Likelihood phylogeny

assessments.G1_reason: Central claim (within-region genetic diversity increases monotonically through the Holocene) is a statistical estimate computed from genotype data: pairwise (1 - f3) distances and Spearman correlation with time.
assessments.G3_note: BAM data at ENA PRJEB51705; genotype Dataset1 and raw figure tables at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6377228. Deposit contents not yet downloaded or verified.
assessments.G4_note: Named tools (AdmixTools, EIGENSOFT, ANGSD, samtools, msprime) are free/open-source; versions reported. Full BAM reprocessing likely exceeds the 4 vCPU/120 min run budget; the Zenodo genotype dataset may suffice for the target.
assessments.G5_note: Methods give tools and parameters but the exact grouping of individuals into regions/time periods and the diversity statistic construction depend on supplementary tables not yet examined.
assessments.target_candidate: Per-region Spearman rho between within-region genetic diversity (mean pairwise 1 - f3) and time period; reported as rho > 0.94, one-sided p < 0.04 in all regions except the Aegean (Figure 4; Zenodo Table Z4).
assessments.alternatives_considered: Inter-regional (1 - f3) differentiation pattern (Figure 5) and X-vs-autosome distance residuals (Figure 6B) were later in order of appearance and less central to the stated summary.

assessments.G1_reason: Central claim is a predictive-evaluation metric (test accuracy of a hybrid CNN + classical-feature classifier on MRI).
assessments.G3_note: ADNI MRI requires an individual data-use application approved by ADNI; the article calls it publicly available via the ADNI access page. Not obtainable by ordinary free registration open to any reader.
assessments.G4_note: Preprocessing/segmentation reported in MATLAB (commercial, version unspecified); CNN in Keras/Python. The described functions are replicable with free tools under the commercial-software policy.
assessments.G5_note: Subject selection from ADNI, exact scan lists and train/validation/test split are not published; the CNN architecture is described but hyperparameters would need assumptions.
assessments.target_candidate: Test-set accuracy for AD vs CN classification = 91.84% (Table 5).
assessments.alternatives_considered: sMCI vs pMCI test accuracy 80.85% (Table 4) is secondary in the abstract's ordering.

evidence.quote: Its test accuracy stood at 91.84% in CN vs AD classification paradigm

assessments.G1_reason: Central claim (numbers of differential urinary proteins between time points/groups) is produced by DIA quantification followed by fold-change and t-test screening.
assessments.G3_note: Mass spectrometry raw data deposited at ProteomeXchange/iProX PXD027610; deposit contents not yet downloaded or verified.
assessments.G4_note: DIA quantification was done with Spectronaut Pulsar X and library search with Proteome Discoverer 2.1 (both commercial). Free alternatives (e.g. DIA-NN, FragPipe) exist but equivalence is not established; the differential-screening step itself (FC >= 1.5 or <= 0.67, p < 0.05) is trivially free.
assessments.G5_note: Database, tolerances and screening thresholds are specified; library-search and DIA settings are partially specified. 69 DIA samples likely exceed the run compute budget if reprocessed from raw.
assessments.target_candidate: Number of differential proteins at W1 vs W0 within the experimental group: 12 upregulated and 15 downregulated (Table 1).
assessments.alternatives_considered: Oil Red O staining area (17.78% vs 0.88%) is a wet-lab measurement; later between-group comparisons appear after Table 1.

assessments.G1_reason: Central dexterity claim (40% fewer movements, reduced path length/time) is computed from video-based marker tracking and movement-feature extraction followed by paired t-tests.
assessments.G3_note: Video/tracking data and code are 'available on reasonable request'; no deposit.
assessments.G4_note: Custom computer-vision tracking software is unpublished; the described marker segmentation and feature extraction are implementable with free tools. SPSS 25 paired t-test is replicable.
assessments.G5_note: Marker segmentation, interpolation/median-filter parameters and movement-count definition are described qualitatively only; without the request-only videos no attempt can proceed past access.
assessments.target_candidate: Reduction in number of movements with Click-On vs DROP-IN probe during the phantom exercise = 40% (Results, Fig. 3).
assessments.alternatives_considered: Tracking accuracy (1.10/0.50/0.88 mm) is a validation metric, not the principal effect; in vivo task-completion increase (60%) appears later.

evidence.quote: movements required to perform the exercise by 40%
Custom computer-vision software was created to segment the markers
paired-samples t test with the SPSS statistical software package

assessments.G1_reason: Central claims are wet-lab measurements (lignin degradation ratios, LiP/MnP enzyme activities, GC-MS product identification). Statistics are mean ± SD and one-way ANOVA/Duncan on unpublished replicates; no central computational transformation.
assessments.alternatives_considered: ANOVA of enzyme activities considered; the reported outputs are measured values whose raw replicates are not reported, so the computation is ancillary.

assessments.G1_reason: Collaboration profile article describing a serosurveillance platform; states no data are associated with the article and presents no central computational result.

evidence.quote: No data are associated with this article

assessments.G1_reason: Mixed-methods study; the headline quantitative result (56.8% perceiving T1D as a barrier) is a proportion of 51 respondents, and the main conclusions are thematic. Chi-square/relative-risk analyses exist but are not the central claim.
assessments.G3_note: Participant-level data available on request only, with privacy restrictions.
assessments.G4_note: SPSS descriptive statistics and chi-square are replicable with free tools.
assessments.target_candidate: Proportion perceiving T1D as a barrier to obesity treatment = 56.8% (Results).
assessments.alternatives_considered: Relative risks of contributory factors (Table) considered; their centrality is unclear.

evidence.quote: available upon request from the corresponding author

assessments.G1_reason: Central claims are statistical associations (Spearman correlations, Mann-Whitney/Wilcoxon tests) between flow-cytometry-derived cell frequencies and antibody titers; reproducing them requires applying the tests to the per-animal values.
assessments.G2_note: Many correlations are reported with equal prominence; the abstract lists several. Target chosen by order of appearance in the abstract; author verification of centrality requested.
assessments.G3_note: Data statement says original contributions are in the article/Supplementary Material; whether per-animal values are tabulated (vs plotted only) has not been verified.
assessments.G4_note: GraphPad Prism statistics are replicable with free tools.
assessments.G5_note: Test choices are named; exact input values, timepoints and handling of ties/one- vs two-sided tests need confirmation from figures/supplement.
assessments.target_candidate: Spearman correlation between LN Env-specific TFH cells post-priming and rectal Env-specific IgA titers (Figure 3F/G and Table 2; abstract order of appearance).
assessments.alternatives_considered: Correlation of GC B cells with vaginal Env-specific IgG; cTFH post-2nd-boost vs viral load; co-culture IgA release (later in abstract).

evidence.quote: correlated negatively with vaginal Env-specific IgG titers but positively with rectal Env-specific IgA titers
included in the article/ Supplementary Material

assessments.G1_reason: Core-genome phylogeny (Roary + IQ-TREE) and lineage-specific gene distribution from 142 sequenced genomes are central computational results alongside wet-lab phenotypes.
assessments.G2_note: The paper mixes epidemiological proportions, phylogeny, gene-presence tables and phenotypes without a single stated primary endpoint. Provisional target chosen as the first objectively assessable genomic table; author verification requested.
assessments.G3_note: Genome sequences under NGDC BioProject PRJCA012518; deposit not yet downloaded or verified.
assessments.G4_note: Roary v3.12.2, IQ-TREE, RAST web annotation, PubMLST, ResFinder are free; GraphPad Prism 8 statistics replicable. RAST version/availability is a web-service dependency.
assessments.G5_note: Tool names given; assembly, annotation and Roary/IQ-TREE parameters largely default/unspecified. 142 genomes through Roary may approach the compute budget.
assessments.target_candidate: Lineage-specific presence of the spl serine protease gene cluster: present only in ST5 and ST239 among the 142 represented ST59/ST398/ST239/ST5 isolates (Fig. 2A).
assessments.alternatives_considered: Decline of ST239 from 15.47% (2013) to 3.35% (2018-2020) is a proportion of isolate counts; core-genome tree topology lacks a numerical comparison rule.

evidence.quote: present only in ST5 and ST239

assessments.G1_reason: Central methodological claim is the performance of SNP-specific Random Forest genotype-calling models (accuracy/sensitivity/OOB error) trained on Fluidigm fluorescence intensities.
assessments.G3_note: Assay description is in the supplement, but the fluorescence-intensity training/test datasets are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request only.
assessments.G4_note: R 4.0.4 and randomForest 4.6-14 are free. Fluidigm hardware is only needed to generate inputs, not to analyse them.
assessments.G5_note: Model features, 50/50 split and filtering thresholds (OOB > 0.05, sensitivity < 0.9) are specified; random seeds, ntree/mtry and control-correction details need confirmation.
assessments.target_candidate: Overall accuracy of the Random Forest genotype calls on experimental Fluidigm pools = 99% (abstract; Fig. 3H).
assessments.alternatives_considered: 96% accuracy vs sequence data; 31 SNP assays passing filters (Fig. 4); 21% accuracy gain from control correction (paired t-test).

evidence.quote: available from the corresponding author on reasonable request

deterministic_candidate_chain.rule: Candidates are consumed in the deterministic hash order of paper2.acquisition.candidate_order. A candidate is skipped only for missing lawfully retained article text or for primary G1/G2 ineligibility, never for reconstruction difficulty. Skipped-for-text candidates remain unadjudicated, not negative.
